$$
\frac{∂w}{∂y}=\frac{∂w}{∂r}\sin \theta+\frac{1}{r}\frac{∂w}{∂\theta}\cos \theta.
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $w$ with respect to $r$ and $\theta:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂w}{∂r}=- 2 r,\,\frac{∂w}{∂\theta}=0\end{aligned}
$$

Then, substituting these into our chain rule formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂w}{∂y} & =(- 2 r)\sin \theta+\frac{1}{r}(0)\cos \theta \\ & =- 2 r \sin {\theta}.\end{aligned}
$$
